selectedModuleReceipts.name: Strategic Planning in Forest and Nature Conservation

reviewedEntryKnowledge.AK: This course builds on knowledge and skills developed in FEM20909  Forest and Nature Conservation II - Management Planning and Tools &  FNP23303  Forest & Nature Conservation Approaches: Theories, Tools and Practices.    From  FEM20909 , students are expected to bring experience with analysing forest and nature areas, comparing management options, and developing management advice based on ecological, spatial and field-based information. From  FNP23303 , students are expected to bring knowledge of different conservation approaches, including ecosystem, landscape and governance-oriented perspectives, and the ability to critically reflect on their advantages, limitations and trade-offs.  In  FNP30306 , these earlier insights are brought together at a regional and landscape level. Students apply ecological, social and governance perspectives to a real transboundary protected-area landscape and develop a strategic action plan for a complex forest and nature conservation challenge.
